Bullock’s Film Room

Note: Unless something changes, this article appears to be unlocked and available to be read from beginning to end

Commanders Film Review: Antonio Williams vs Eagles

[Note: The play described in the excerpt below is embedded in the tweet posted in the body of the article]

Commanders head coach Dan Quinn singled out rookie wide receiver Antonio Williams as someone that he thought could step up and play a bigger role after star receiver Terry McLaurin suffered a season-ending injury a few weeks ago. Against the Eagles, Williams certainly didn’t disappoint. He caught five passes for 54 yards and could have had plenty more too. The Eagles have a strong secondary but every corner that faced him struggled to stick close.

There were a number of key traits that stood out from Williams in this game and I’ll try and cover them all in this post. First, let’s start with the most important thing, his hands. Williams displayed good hands throughout the game, making some tough adjustments to pull in passes that weren’t perfectly accurate. He often did it in a way that made you quickly forget the ball wasn’t perfect too, which I’m sure his quarterback appreciates.

This play is a great example of the combination of all of the traits we’ve seen from Williams in this post so far. He shows good speed, good route running, and great hands. Williams begins this play as the outside receiver to the right of the formation, but he’s aligned tight to the formation. Initially, he has cornerback Quinyon Mitchell lined up opposite him, but that soon changes. The Commanders motion tight end Chig Okonkwo outside of Williams, making Williams the slot receiver. The Eagles react by bumping Mitchell outside over Okonkwo, while the safety rotates down from deep to cover Williams.

That’s a strong matchup for the Commanders and one Williams takes full advantage of. Williams runs a double move against the safety. He initially angles his route outside and gets all the way to the edge of the numbers as he fully sells his fake break outside. This commitment to the fake forces the safety to bite on it, which enables Williams to burst past him. Williams opens up a gap of five yards on the safety very quickly and Daniels pulls the trigger. His throw is a little lofty and Williams has to slow down as he tracks the ball in the air. But he makes a nice adjustment to work back to the ball, jumping up to grab the ball before the safety could get there. He bobbles the pass slightly but manages to secure the ball as the safety lands a big hit, completing the 30-yard gain.

It was an impressive outing from the rookie receiver and one that means he now leads the Commanders receivers with 259 receiving yards from 23 catches so far this season. If he continues to play this well, those numbers should only grow. He’s definitely worthy of a bigger role and more targets within the offense, especially without McLaurin. He’s doing a great job on the outside as the Z receiver but he’s also very capable of playing the same role as Diggs in the slot.

I wonder if we’ll see him shift inside a little more often in key situations as the season progresses, trusting him to make some of those critical plays in big spots that Diggs is making. Diggs has been a great signing so far, but Williams is the future, so I wonder if we’ll see a passing of the torch at some point. For now though, with Burks playing McLaurin’s X receiver role, Williams can claim the Z receiver role as his own and he should only become an increasingly larger part of the offense going forward.

More from Sports Illustrated:

Snap Judgment: Williams (50 snaps – 83%) led the receivers in playing time, ahead of Burks (40 snaps – 67%) and Diggs (39 snaps – 65%). I’d keep him at the front of this rotation.

Williams caught three passes for 20 yards on Washington’s 89-yard touchdown drive. His five-yard catch on third-and-4 kept the possession alive, and a 10-yard reception on second-and-10 moved the chains again. In the fourth quarter, his 30-yard catch was the biggest gain on the drive that pushed Washington’s lead to 19-10.

Sports Illustrated

Five Sacks Without Three DTs

Washington’s defensive front supplied the answer it needed most. Daron Payne, Javon Kinlaw and Jer’Zhan Newton were all unavailable, but the Commanders sacked Tanner McKee five times and held Saquon Barkley to 30 yards on 13 carries. Charles Omenihu returned with a sack, three quarterback hits and a fumble recovery. Quinn said Monday the rush looked more coordinated and connected after the staff made it a focus during the bye. With Payne’s foot injury reportedly ending his season, Washington will need that work to hold up beyond one game.

More from Sports Illustrated:

Snap Judgment: Omenihu played 46 defensive snaps (67%), compared with 49 for K’Lavon Chaisson, 45 for Odafe Oweh and 40 for Dorance Armstrong. I’d keep him involved when the front gets healthier.

Omenihu was also credited with a quarterback hit on the fourth-down pass Rasul Douglas intercepted late in the fourth quarter. Douglas returned it to Philadelphia’s 37, and Washington scored on its next possession.

Commanders.com

Game Balls | 4 standouts from Washington’s win against the Eagles

Treylon Burks

Burks’ shook off his first error on Sunday night — a dropped pass on third-and-3 — and went on to have one of his best games to date in burgundy and gold. The wide receiver led the team in receiving yards in the win and torched Philadelphia’s secondary as a deep threat for Daniels.

In the first quarter, he showed length to stretch out for a seven-yard pass that resulted in an important first-down conversion with Washington down 10. In the second quarter, he ran a comeback route out to the right and brought in the ball for a 21-yard gain before being pushed out of bounds.

His biggest catch of the night came in the third quarter. Burks got the better of Quinyon Mitchell downfield and hauled in a 53-yard pass from Daniels. The catch was the longest reception by a Washington player this season. There’s no replacing McLaurin, but Burks filled in a gap left by the number one wide receiver’s absence and proved he can influence the game in big ways when called upon.

5 takeaways from Commanders vs. Eagles

Daniels was solid in his first win in over a year

There were some parallels between Daniels’ last win, which came on Oct. 5, 2025, against the Los Angeles Chargers, and Sunday’s victory. In both games, the Commanders gave their opponents a 10-0 lead before going on a tear to get the win.

And like the rest of the team, it took Daniels some time to find a groove, but he ended the night with another solid performance.

“I see a lot from him in the poise and the location of where to throw deep shots,” Quinn said.

Daniels led the Commanders to a field goal drive after addressing the offense, but he did not really look like himself until the following possession. Riggo’s Rag

Drew Stevens gives Commanders reason to believe their kicker search is over

Drew Stevens, Washington’s undrafted rookie kicker, nailed four of five attempts, including a momentum-swinging 56-yarder late in the first quarter. All in all, the Iowa product has been money this season from anything within 50 yards, and he’s got the leg to hit from distance.

Stevens started shaky and has missed three extra points this season. But he did a lot of growing up on Sunday night, and now it’s all about how he’s able to build on it.

A kicker’s primary job is to be someone who won’t lose you the game. But great kickers can actively be the reason you win a game. Stevens was one reason Washington beat the Eagles, continuing his encouraging form after some early jitters.

No other position in the NFL is as driven by confidence as kicker. For Stevens, who missed a 55-yarder on Washington’s opening drive, he could have spiraled into disaster when head coach Dan Quinn placed him in the same situation from one yard further later in the opening frame.

Instead, Stevens drilled it, which turned into a springboard for his best game of the season.

By the end of the night, Stevens accounted for 13 of Washington’s 27 points, outscoring the Eagles by himself.

Jeremy McNichols will be sidelined for months

Veteran Jeremy McNichols is expected to miss several months while reports broke on Monday that he is seeking additional opinions into Tuesday. McNichols suffered what was reported as a mid-foot injury in Sunday’s win over the Philadelphia Eagles.

It marks the latest blow to the running back room with position coach Anthony Lynn Jr. also adjusting without Jacory Croskey-Merritt, who remains on injured reserve after suffering a groin injury in week five.

How the Commanders adjust in the running back room remains to be seen with Rachaad White, who registered his lone rushing touchdown on Sunday night, currently ranked third on the team with 200 rushing yards on 47 attempts. Austin Ekeler has also loomed large as a mid-season signing for Washington where he owns 67 rushing yards on 16 carries through four games. 7 running backs who could help the Commanders survive their injury crisis

Commanders could sign Jerome Ford

With the Washington Commanders needing someone who can step in and provide immediate help, turning to someone already familiar with the setup may be the best path. That brings Jerome Ford under the microscope.

Ford joined the Commanders in free agency this offseason after falling behind Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson during his final season with the Cleveland Browns. Things didn’t go well, mainly due to injuries, and he was eventually waived with an injury designation.

The Minnesota Vikings signed him to their practice squad, but released him soon after. Ford wasn’t out of work for long, and he’s currently on the Arizona Cardinals’ practice squad waiting for his opportunity.

He is reportedly healthy now, too. Ford knows David Blough’s scheme and the locker room culture, so the transition would be smooth. And with the Commanders needing help right now, he may be on their shortlist.

Commanders could sign Khalil Herbert

Unlike most players on this list, Khalil Herbert has actually seen some regular-season action during the 2026 campaign. He’s been called up twice from the Atlanta Falcons’ practice squad, but another elevation would mean he needs to be signed to their 53-man roster.

That might be something the struggling NFC South club is reluctant to do. Therefore, the Commanders could make that decision for them by making him an offer.

Herbert is a pocket rocket. While he lacks the size and physicality to be a legitimate three-down force, he is a nice change-of-pace option who can also help on passing downs. This is similar to how the Commanders deploy Jeremy McNichols, so it could be a nice like-for-like possibility to consider.

The 2021 sixth-round pick out of Virginia Tech looked like a potential star earlier in his career with the Chicago Bears. Things have tailed off for Herbert since, but he could definitely help Washington in the short term.

item.title: Giants are betting favorite to win NFC East, and have John Harbaugh to thank
item.description: Veteran had coach has driven Giants to the point of having an unexpected opportunity.
item.content:encoded:
The New York Giants are now the betting favorite to win the NFC East, per FanDuel Sportsbook. The 4-2-1 division-leading Giants are -134 to win their first division title since 2011. The Dallas Cowboys are +220, the Washington Commanders +400, and the Philadelphia Eagles +1600.

The struggles of the division’s other three underachieving teams have opened the door for the Giants. Head coach John Harbaugh, though, deserves most of the credit. Harbaugh, the $100 million coach the Giants successfully courted after the Baltimore Ravens fired him following 18 seasons, made his team believe it could do what it has done so far.

Harbaugh, 63, gave a huge hint of what was to come at his introductory press conference in January. Asked if he considered taking a year off from coaching after the Ravens let him go, Harbaugh scoffed at the idea.

“I figured I didn’t have enough time to take time off,” Harbaugh said. “There’s no time for that, so just couldn’t wait to get back to work. That was never a question.”

There is something else Harbaugh doesn’t have time for. Rebuilding, or accepting that circumstances — like major injuries at crucial positions — will derail hopes of a good season.

“We have an opportunity to go win, and I like these players, man,” Harbaugh said at that introductory press conference. “I know they want to be successful and they want to go to work, so absolutely we can do that, and that’s our plan to do that. The plan is to win every game. I mean, one game at a time. You go into every game planning to win that game. That’s our expectation.”

Harbaugh has driven the Giants to have the best, most productive day possible every day. Harbaugh’s Giants put in as many hours and practice as hard as the rules will allow.

“You do the best you can with it every single day. Well, that means a lot when you really think about what that means,” Harbaugh said. “Are we really doing our best? Are we really putting everything we have into it for this day? Are we really attacking the day with an enthusiasm unknown to mankind? Another level? Is that possible? Is that something that we can accomplish? Can we have the best meeting and the best practice in the history of the National Football League? Can we? When you do that day by day, you build something, you take it onto the field, and you let the chips fly, and you go play some ball.”

So far, a lot of the chips have fallen in the Giants’ favor.

In 18 seasons in Baltimore, Harbaugh’s teams made the playoffs 12 times, had just three losing seasons, and won a Super Bowl. He did not have to convince anyone he knew what he was doing.

“It started from day one in the spring. Coach (John Harbaugh) came in here and just the details, the messaging, the leadership. His record speaks for itself as a head coach. The guy has won a lot of games,” GM Joe Schoen said during the bye week. “The players were eager to buy in. We have a good, young nucleus of players here that just want to win. Just want to win, whatever it takes. Coach Harbaugh and his staff have done a very good job of laying out the plan. This is what it looks like. This is how you practice. This is how you approach OTA’s. This is how you approach the offseason program. This is how you train in training camp. This is how you prepare in-season, week to week.”

  • If Harbaugh were building instead of trying to win as often as possible, he probably wouldn’t have brought so many ex-Ravens with him.
  • Giving 33-year-old Odell Beckham a chance, even though it didn’t work out, was about trying to field the best team Harbaugh could right now.
  • Trading for J.J. McCarthy after Jaxson Dart’s Week 2 season-ending injury was a clear sign that Harbaugh wasn’t tossing in the towel on the season, despite whatever long-term quarterback drama that move eventually brings with it.
  • Going after Jeffery Simmons and Jonathan Taylor on the trade market is about capitalizing on the opportunity the Giants have, not building for a better tomorrow.

Who can challenge the Giants?

None of the Giants’ NFC East challengers have had the seasons they imagined. I asked the lead writers from Blogging the Boys (Cowboys), Bleeding Green Nation (Eagles), and Hogs Haven (Commanders) for thoughts on whether they felt their teams could challenge for the crown, and who would eventually win the division.

At 3-5, Dallas is in second place. The Cowboys already have a loss to the Giants. They have losses to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Arizona Cardinals. They haven’t fixed their defensive issues, with young defensive coordinator Christian Parker looking like he might not be ready for the job. Owner Jerry Jones is being asked about head coach Brian Schottenheimer’s future.

Despite that, R.J. Ochoa of Blogging the Boys is still a believer that the Cowboys will pull themselves together and win the division.

“The Dallas Cowboys will in the most basic, bare bones, literal way possible.

“I say this because of the non-Giants teams in the division; the Cowboys might be the least fallible. On paper, the Cowboys have pieces that comprise contending/challenging teams, but they have not been anything close to their on-paper version so far this season.

“They deserve no benefit of the doubt right now. Everyone keeps believing they will put together a little run to make “challenging” a thing, but they are losing to hapless teams like the Buccaneers and Cardinals.

“Congratulations to the Giants on a successful start to the John Harbaugh era.

The Eagles, entering Sunday’s game with the Giants, have lost a stunning six games in a row. They have lost an immense amount of talent, including quarterback Jalen Hurts to injury. They have traded away players like A.J. Brown and Cam Jurgens, and watched right tackle Lane Johnson retire during the season.

Brandon Lee Gowton of Bleeding Green Nation is taking the Cowboys to emerge as champs.

“The Eagles will not.

“The Eagles are arguably the worst team in the NFL. It’s hard to see how things are going to get better for them this season.

“The Giants certainly have a good energy going for them as they currently sit atop the division. But quarterback uncertainty remains. The Cowboys could eventually wake up; they have the NFL’s sixth-easiest remaining schedule. I’ll take Dallas to very narrowly edge the Giants.”

The 2-4-1 Commanders lost quarterback Jayden Daniels for two games, and have been beset by clock management issues. It is hard to count them out, though.

As the Giants return from their bye, they have games against the Eagles and Commanders in five days. Harbaugh knows what they mean.

“The two most important games of the season will be coming up after we come back from the bye, which will

set the direction for the rest of the season really,” Harbaugh said after the Week 7 victory over the Houston Texans.

item.title: Cam Skattebo injury: Giants’ RB a question mark heading into game vs. Eagles
item.description: Cam Skattebo is working through an injury as he tries to suit up for the New York Giants in Week 9.
item.content:encoded:
Even after the bye week, New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo is still dealing with a hamstring injury he suffered during the team’s Week 7 overtime win against the Houston Texans. Skattebo did not practice on Monday as the team returned to work.

Skattebo broke off a 42-yard run in overtime that helped the Giants pull out a win, but it came at a price, as he picked up a hamstring injury. Giants head coach John Harbaugh spoke about Skattebo’s injury in more detail.

“It’s going to be probably day to day up to the game,” Harbaugh said. ”We’re going to just have to see where we’re at. I’ll probably have more information toward the end of the week. We’ll see on both those guys where we’re at.“

Skattebo has had an up-and-down season for the Giants. He scored a touchdown in the team’s Week 1 win against the Dallas Cowboys, but struggled to find the end zone in the next four weeks. He also recorded four fumbles in the team’s first five games.

His struggles led to him being benched in the team’s Week 6 loss against the New Orleans Saints, but he redeemed himself against the Texans when he had his best game of the season. He ran 17 times for 124 yards and a touchdown to help the Giants pull out a big win on the road.

Skattebo likely will have a big role when the team plays the Philadelphia Eagles this week if he is able to go.

Should Skattebo have to sit out, it will mean an extended opportunity for Devin Singletary and newly-signed Gregory Desrosiers. Eric Gray, who was just signed to the practice squad, and Phil Mafah are running backs who would be available for elevation.

item.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: RBs in timeshares you can trust in Week 9 lineups
item.description: Fred Zinkie offers start/sit lineup advice for some of the top RB2s in fantasy football going into Week 9.
item.content:encoded:
Let's take a look at RB2s in backfield splits, who are listed in the order that they should be started in Week 9. Current roster rates on Yahoo are listed in parentheses.

Note: Braelon Allen has graduated from this list, as his success in the absence of Breece Hall could cause him to remain the starter when Hall returns to action.

5 RB2s who can help you in Week 9

1. Jonah Coleman, Broncos (73%)

Week 8 couldn't have worked out much better for Coleman. The Broncos trailed the Chiefs for most of the game, which caused Sean Payton to take the drastic step of benching starter J.K. Dobbins by halftime. Dobbins logged just one snap and zero touches in the second half, while Coleman took over the backfield in a comeback victory that moved the Broncos ahead of the Chiefs in the AFC West standings. Coleman rewarded his coach for the additional opportunities by logging a 51-yard reception and a five-yard touchdown run on the team's final drive of the game.

Although the Broncos' official depth chart lists Coleman behind Dobbins and injured RB RJ Harvey, it's clear that this is Coleman's backfield now. He's easily an RB2 option for a Week 9 matchup against a Panthers defense that has allowed the second-most fantasy points per game to opposing running backs. The one caveat for putting in an aggressive offer for Coleman on the Yahoo Trade Market is the rumor that the Broncos will attempt to acquire Colts RB Jonathan Taylor by the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

2. Blake Corum, Rams (84%)

At first glance, things were status quo in the Rams backfield during Week 8, with Kyren Williams receiving 16 carries in comparison to 11 for Corum. But a closer look reveals that with seven minutes left in the game and the Rams leading 24-9, Williams had logged just five carries. He was used to run out the clock in a lopsided victory over the winless Chargers, while Corum carried the ball more when the game was in doubt.

Maintaining a roughly even split in the Rams backfield is working well, as Williams has averaged 4.9 yards per carry and Corum has produced a 5.2 mark. While it was surprising to see Corum receiving a heavier workload for most of the Week 8 win, it would be premature to dismiss Williams as the team's lead runner. Both players should be ranked among the top-20 RB options for a favorable Week 9 matchup against a Commanders defense that has been average against the run, but has allowed the seventh-most points per game.

3. Mike Washington Jr., Raiders (28%)

Although the critics were lining up for Ashton Jeanty throughout the days leading up to the Week 8 game against the Jets, it was still shocking to see Washington receive 25 carries in comparison to just two rushes for Jeanty. As per usual, Jeanty was heavily involved in the passing game (3-64), while Washington was not targeted.

Washington was stopped four times at the goal line, which contributed to an average of 3.3 yards per carry. Still, the Raiders won for the first time in over a month, and their offense produced 38 points. Perhaps this was similar to the Cam Skattebo situation, where the coaching staff was trying to get the attention of the lead back by dramatically cutting his workload. Or perhaps the Raiders will leave things status quo after a big win and give Washington most of the carries against the 49ers in Week 9.

Washington's upside is somewhat limited by a tough matchup against a San Francisco defense that ranks fifth in rushing yards allowed per game and his lack of involvement in the passing game. But the potential volume on the ground will keep him ranked around RB25, which makes him a borderline RB2.

4. Kyle Monangai, Bears* (74%)

Monangai missed a fourth straight game with toe and thumb injuries in Week 8, which has surprised fantasy managers and the Bears. After all, Chicago almost certainly would have put Monangai on injured reserve weeks ago if it expected him to miss four games. Given that the hard-charging runner has missed more time than expected, we can assume that he may finally return to action this week.

Monangai may be the Bears’ best pure runner. He perfectly combines a physical running style with the potential for long runs. D'Andre Swift has done his best to handle a heavy workload in Monangai's absence, averaging 3.2 yards on 74 carries over the past four games. With the team coming off a short week, head coach Ben Johnson will surely be open to reducing Swift's workload, which would make Monangai an appealing flex option against the Bucs this week, if he returns. Although the Bucs are excellent against the run, a Bears offense that ranks second in rushing yards per game will give them their toughest test thus far. Make sure to monitor Monangai’s status in practice this week closely.

5. Tyler Allgeier, Cardinals (52%)

Allgeier may have been the best story of Week 8. Injuries suffered in the first half by Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Bam Knight (concussion) left Allgeier as the team's only healthy option in a game where they were consistently trailing the Cowboys. The former Falcon put the team on his back down the stretch, scoring on a 63-yard run and a five-yard reception, where he made an impressive stretch to reach the goal line. After Allgeier sparked the offense, Trey McBride and Michael Wilson made big plays of their own and finished off one of the most improbable OT wins of the season.

The Cardinals could place Love on IR, as he has dealt with multiple right ankle injuries, dating back to August. Knight may also be absent in Week 9 while he recovers from his concussion. The coaching staff already prefers Allgeier in passing situations and may give him most of the rushing work as well. Unfortunately, the Cardinals are double-digit underdogs for their road game in Seattle. Arizona will have one of the lowest projected point totals, which limits Allgeier to being a flex option.

Five more for deep leagues

The following players will rank outside the top 25 running backs in Week 9 but can be expected to tally 5-10 points for those who are desperate.

1. Woody Marks, Texans (79%)

The Texans could get David Montgomery (groin) back for Week 9, which would relegate Marks to a backup role that carries notable volume. Marks could convert 5-8 carries and a couple catches into a decent fantasy performance, as the Texans will face the winless Chargers, who are below average in rushing yards and points allowed per game.

2. Aaron Jones Sr., Vikings (88%)

The Vikings continue to deploy Jones and Jordan Mason in an even split. In Week 8, Mason logged three more carries than Jones, while Jones caught two more passes than Mason. Minnesota's next game will take place on Monday Night Football against the high-scoring Bills. Jones should get 7-10 touches in that game, and his role in the passing game makes him slightly more valuable in PPR formats.

3. Kaelon Black, 49ers (31%)

Some managers may have forgotten that Black gained 53 yards and scored a touchdown on 12 carries in Week 7 before the 49ers enjoyed their Week 8 bye. The team returns to action for a favorable home matchup against the Raiders. Most prediction models have the team as double-digit favorites with an expected point total around 30. If those predictions are realized, Black will likely get 8-10 touches.

4. Jadarian Price, Seahawks (68%)

The Seahawks’ official website listed Zach Charbonnet as the starter as soon as he was activated from IR. But it was Price who led the RB room in touches in a Monday Night Football loss to the Bears, tallying 10 carries and two receptions. The rookie and his teammates did little with their opportunities, as the Bears defense, led by recent acquisition Jeffery Simmons, turned the clock back to 1985 and dominated the line of scrimmage. Price and the entire offense should be more successful in a Week 9 home game in which Seattle is a double-digit favorite over Arizona.

5. Kenny Gainwell, Bucs (42%)

Over the past two weeks, Tampa Bay has turned the clock back 50 years by tallying 105 rushes and 14 passes, with Gainwell reviving his season by rushing for 228 yards on 39 carries. Starter Bucky Irving has been outstanding as well, and the Bucs will likely try to assert themselves on the ground in Week 9, when they travel to Chicago to face the Bears. Chicago has been excellent against the run but will be coming off a short week and could be more vulnerable than usual to a physical attack.

10 Backup RBs to Stash

item.title: Ben Johnson: Jeffery Simmons has fit right in, he got a game ball
item.description: Fresh off last week's trade from the Titans to the Bears, defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons had a clear impact on Monday night's win over the Seahawks.
item.content:encoded:
Fresh off last week's trade from the Titans to the Bears, defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons had a clear impact on Monday night's win over the Seahawks.

Simmons finished the game with six tackles, two tackles for loss, a sack, and a pass defensed in the 34-17 victory.

Head coach Ben Johnson told reporters after the game that he gave Simmons a game ball or the performance.

“Our guys were excited the moment they heard the news we were bringing him on, and he's fit right in,” Johnson said. "We have a high-character locker room, and he's that himself. You can feel his presence out there, whether it's during the play or even after the play. You can feel him talk a little smack as well which I think that elevates everybody around him.

“I thought he played outstanding. He got one of the game balls. To come in there and have a share of the lead of tackles and a sack in his first game, his impact was profound.”

The Bears allowed just 252 total yards on Monday night, which was 1 yard off from Seattle’s lowest output of the season. The Bears will be at home to play the Buccaneers on Sunday night in Week 9.

item.title: Bears vs. Seahawks: Inside the Snap Counts, Stats, and Jefe’s Big Game
item.description: Here are the Bears' snap counts, stats, and more from their big win over the Seahawks, from @wiltfongjr.
item.content:encoded:
The Chicago Bears beat the Seattle Seahawks by 17 points. This was the first time the Seahawks lost a game by more than 4 points since December 15, 2024. Chicago’s 34 to 17 victory was their third consecutive 30-point output this season. But as good as the offense was, this game was about the new-look defense thanks to Jeffery Simmons.

“We got a high-character locker room, and he (Simmons) is that himself,” head coach Ben Johnson said about his newest player after the game. “And you can feel his presence out there, whether it’s during the play or even after the play; you can feel him talking a little smack as well, which I think that elevates everybody around him. So I thought he played outstanding. To come in there and have a share of the lead of tackles and a sack in his first game, his impact was profound.”

In his postgame interviews, quarterback Caleb Williams called Simmons “Jefe,” Spanish for boss. I’m not sure if that’s a new nickname or if it came over from Tennessee, but it fits the dominant Simmons.

Caleb was asked what it’s like watching Jerrery Simmons play football.

“I’m happy he’s… It’s Jefe… I’m happy he’s on our side,” Williams said. “He helps everybody on that field on the defense. He helps the D-line when he gets double teams. He frees up other guys to be able to go be special. And then when he gets one-on- ones, he, you know, allows him to wreak havoc. I’m excited he’s on our team. He’s a big key piece for us.”

The Bears outgained the Seahawks (363 yards to 252), had more first downs (22 to 18), won the time of possession (35:03 to 24:57), and ran more plays (70 to 56).

The Bears were better on third down (46.7% to 9.1%) and went 1 for 1 on fourth down, while Seattle went 1 for 2 on fourth down. The Bears also committed more penalties (10 for 85 yards to 5 for 43), but the turnovers were equal with 1 each.

Let’s look at the Bears’ playing-time breakdown and a few individual stats from the game.

OFFENSE

From our guy Ken Mitchell (on Twitter @WCGBearsDenDude), Caleb entered last night’s game against Seattle tied with Aaron Rodgers at 35 consecutive regular-season games with no more than one interception and at least 20 pass attempts. And with 34 attempts and no picks, the NFL record is now 36.

Seattle’s defense has stymied opposing quarterbacks all season, with none of them passing for more than 189 yards in a game, but Williams was patient; he pushed the ball downfield when he had the chance and also worked the quick game.

DEFENSE

Jeffery Simmons made an even bigger impact than I hoped. ESPN shared a graphic after the game that in the plays with Simmons on the field the Seahawks averaged 3 yards per play, and in the plays with him on the sideline, they averaged 13.3. The Bears held Seattle to just 1-for-11 on third downs, and that one conversion came with Simmons not on the field.

According to Tej Seth, who pulled some data from Sumer Sports, “With Jeffery Simmons, the Bears blitz rate dropped from 41% coming into this week to 25% in this game. Despite that, they were still able to generate pressure at around the same rate they had been this season while getting to keep more players in coverage.”

This is the first time Simmons has played on a winning team since December 11, 2022.

SPECIAL TEAMS*

*The above image has players who only played in the third phase.

Cairo Santos was perfect on the night, hitting all 4 extra points and all 3 field goals.

Tory Taylor punted 3 times for a 49.0 average (45.0 net average), and one was blocked.

Zavion Thomas returned 4 kicks for 88 yards.

Kalif Raymond returned 2 punts for 7 yards.

Austin Booker blocked a field goal.

Noah Sewell and Daniel Hardy each had 2 special teams tackles.

To check out the complete Bears vs. Seahawks box score, I find ESPN’s site is easy to navigate.

All statistics and snap counts, as well as the accompanying pictures, are taken directly from the NFL’s Game Statistic and Information System.

item.title: Jerry Jones wants to see more targets for George Pickens
item.description: The 3-5 Cowboys have plenty of problems.
item.content:encoded:
The 3-5 Cowboys have plenty of problems. During the first of his two weekly radio spots on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, owner and G.M. Jerry Jones mentioned one specific thing that he'd like to see change.

Regarding receiver George Pickens, Jones said this, via Jon Machota of The Athletic: "He needs the ball coming his way more."

Through eight games, Pickens has 62 targets. In Week 8 against the Cardinals, Pickens had the ball thrown in his direction only four times. Against the Eagles in Week 7, Pickens had six targets.

He has 39 catches for 533 yards and two touchdowns in 2026. That projects to 83 catches for 1,132 yards and 8.5 touchdowns.

In 2025, Pickens finished with 93 receptions, 1,429 yards, and nine scores.

Hovering over the situation is the decision the Cowboys will have to make after the season. He's making $27.298 million under the franchise tag; they could tag him again next year, at $32.758 million. Which is still nearly $10 million behind the top of the receiver market.

There's another option, now that the Cowboys are fading in the race for the NFC East title. They could make Pickens available in trade.

Would a contender offer a second-round pick for him? The Chiefs are currently desperate for help at receiver; they're interested (we're told) in Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. and Colts receiver Josh Downs. If the Chiefs are in on Pickens, other teams in the AFC (like the Bills) should be thinking about it, too.
bi
If the Cowboys were to decide to make a move, they could stockpile a pick or two — and save $15.17 million in cash and cap space. For now, who knows? The Cowboys seem to be deluding themselves into thinking they're still contenders.

Unless that's just part of the annual effort to keep their fans coughing up cash for tickets and merch. Which continues to work very well, relative to the on-field production.

For 31 years, and counting.

item.title: Eagles News: Chris Kuper could be in trouble
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles news and links for 11/3/26.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

Speaking on Monday, Nick Sirianni said the Eagles aren’t going to make any changes. But just because he said that publicly doesn’t mean things could be happening behind the scenes. Something’s gotta give with the team losing six straight and not showing signs of getting better. The Eagles’ offensive line looks like they don’t know what they’re doing.

Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

Short Term Stuff – Iggles Blitz

It really is hard to judge Sean Mannion accurately. He’s had to deal with an insane amount of injuries. The players all speak highly of him. There haven’t been guys ripping him to the media on the record and we aren’t hearing complaints from anonymous sources. At the same time, the offense is historically bad. They can’t be ignored. I would leave Mannion in place for now. The bye week is coming up soon. That will give them a chance to really focus on self-scouting and try to find some fixes. Chris Kuper has also been dealt a tough hand. He thought he was getting 4/5ths of the OL that led the team to a SB win in 2024. Oops. Two of them are no longer with the team. He has already had multiple starters at LG, C, and RG. Jeff Stoutland had injuries last year and the OL wasn’t good so this is not all on Kuper. Still, the confusion and blown blocking assignments is something new. And that is on Kuper.

Eagles-Commanders what we learned: Offensive line miscues should build pressure on Chris Kuper – PHLY Eagles

During his Monday news conference, Sirianni said he won’t make changes to the coaching staff roles. He also defended Kuper’s effort behind the scenes. “We’re not coaching well enough right now and we’re not playing well enough right now,” Sirianni said Monday. “I know we’re speaking offensively. Right now we’re not doing all the things we need to do to win football games. And that falls on everyone’s shoulders. … Chris is coaching his ass off. He’s fighting his ass off. He’s coaching his ass off on a daily basis. You guys don’t get to see that on a daily basis. You get to see it for three hours on Sunday. … I know he’s giving players good tools to use fundamentally and helping them become the best players they possibly can be.” It might make more sense to wait until after this Sunday’s matchup against the New York Giants to take advantage of the following bye week before making changes, but there’s a legitimate argument that the Eagles pass protection calls are currently limiting the team from actually evaluating the group for the future.

Eagles vs. Commanders: The good, the bad, and the ugly – BGN

It was revealed last week that numerous sources in and around the Eagles told Bleeding Green Nation that they still trusted and believed in head coach Nick Sirianni and Fangio. That Sirianni still had the locker room. They still somehow believed that Sirianni could turn around this disaster, because he proved he could win. But where there was once unbending support for learning-on-the-job offensive coordinator Sean Mannion and offensive line coach Chris Kuper, that was bending. It has changed to doubt as the Eagles kept sinking. Mannion simply seems overwhelmed. Kuper can’t foresee where unblocked pressures could come from. That was last week. Let’s make a very strong—but very correct assumption—Mannion and Kuper will not be here next season. Maybe sooner than that. Maybe.

13 young Eagles worth watching in what’s left of a lost season – NBCSP

QB Joe Milton: Maybe the Eagles really do just ride it out with backup quarterback Tanner McKee in place of Jalen Hurts. But there’s some definite intrigue with Milton. The Eagles signed him off the Cowboys’ practice squad on Oct. 16 and it didn’t take long for Milton to supplant Cole Payton as the new backup. The 26-year-old Milton (6-5, 236) has played in just five career games but the former sixth-round pick has plenty of arm talent. His highlight reel from his 2023 season at Tennessee is littered with highlight plays. Milton has a big arm and can elude pressure. He just wasn’t very consistent. But in this lost season, if McKee continues to struggle, it would be fun to see Milton get a chance.

NFC Hierarchy/Obituary: Week 9 edition – PhillyVoice

In Week 5, the Eagles probably played their best game of the season in a loss to the Jaguars, but it was also the week where they may have failed spectacularly as an organization, allowing Jalen Hurts to board two intercontinental flights to and from London and play in a game despite knowing that he had a superficial blood clot in his leg. He would eventually be diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis (“DVT”) and bilateral pulmonary emboli (blood clots in the lungs). His season was over at that point. Investigations into what exactly happened from a medical perspective are most certainly not over. And then the last three games, without Hurts, the Eagles got their teeth kicked in by a trio of teams that have a combined 5-12-1 record this season when they don’t get to play the Eagles. Against those three teams, the Eagles got outscored by 43 points and outgained by 343 yards.

Seven things Solak thinks for NFL Week 9: Bucs atop NFC South? RB trades coming? – ESPN

This trade would be a massive win for the Eagles.

Eagles trade TE Johnny Mundt and a 2027 seventh-round pick to the Vikings for a 2027 sixth-round pick. The Vikings might be a headliner for Jonathan Taylor-trade hype, but my sense is that they’re really looking for a strong blocking tight end after the season-ending injury to Josh Oliver in Week 3. Mundt was in Minnesota from 2022 to 2024 with coach Kevin O’Connell and is currently losing his TE2 job in Philadelphia, as rookie Eli Stowers and veteran Grant Calcaterra return from injured reserve. Mundt played 13 snaps in the Eagles’ loss to the Commanders on Sunday night, his season low. He’ll give the Vikings more reliable point-of-attack blocking for a nominal price.

Eagles’ odds to pick No. 1 overall in the NFL draft are stronger than you think. That makes QB the only question. – Inquirer

The reality of the Eagles’ present moment is one that can define their next 5 to 10 years. After another listless performance in a 27-10 loss to the Commanders, the Eagles are almost surely going to end up with a draft pick in the realm where franchise quarterbacks are most often selected. They have a very real chance at landing the No. 1 overall pick. If they don’t earn it outright, they could have an opportunity to trade for it. If they don’t have an opportunity to trade for the pick itself, they could have an opportunity to trade for the incumbent quarterback of the team that does wind up with the pick. Right now, pole position belongs to the Chargers, who also happen to have a 28-year-old quarterback who has received MVP votes. This is not an argument that Justin Herbert is a better quarterback than Hurts. It certainly isn’t an argument that his resume is better. Likewise for Drew Mestemaker, or CJ Carr, or Arch Manning, or any of the other college quarterbacks who mock drafts have targeted as potential first-round picks. The argument is that the Eagles must decide where they stand in each of these individual cases. It’s not even an argument. It’s just the way an organization must handle its business, same as every year. Except, this year, they are bad enough to be in a position where they must actually decide.

NFL Insider Jason La Canfora Week 9 Notebook: Eagles Trade Rumors, Chiefs Eye Mailata – Casino.org

As for a trade for Mailata, the same GM claimed: “That would be a blockbuster trade. You have to protect the quarterback, no matter who that is next year, and that’s a damn good tackle who has a lot of good football left to play.” The Chiefs may be the team to watch with Mailata, who has effectively a veteran-minimum salary and is signed through 2028. Kansas City head coach Andy Reid spent the first half of his Hall of Fame career in Philadelphia, and he has had a lot of upheaval on his offensive line. Now, suddenly free-agent running back Kenneth Walker isn’t on a record pace anymore, and the Chiefs will be making multiple moves ahead of the deadline as we hear it. But the price would have to be high. “Andy isn’t going to sit on his hands,” said one longtime personnel exec who knows Reid well. “He knows he needs help on offense.”

Saquon Barkley’s commitment to the Eagles is impressive – PFT

The Eagles won’t be trading running back Saquon Barkley. For most players on teams that are falling apart, the inability to chase a championship with a high-end contender would be viewed as bad news. Barkley’s comments after Philly’s latest loss make it clear that he welcomes the opportunity to stick around. It’s impressive that Barkley is committed to a seemingly lost cause. Of course, the decision not to trade Barkley doesn’t mean the team is committed to Barkley for as long as he wants to play in Philadelphia.

NFC playoff picture: NY Giants lead in NFC East widens – Big Blue View

The New York Giants get back to work on Monday with a solid hold on first place in the NFC East entering Week 9. The Giants are 4-2-1, and the division results on Sunday worked out in their favor while they were on their bye week. The 3-5 Dallas Cowboys missed an opportunity gain ground of the Giants on Sunday, blowing a 14-point fourth-quarter lead and losing to the Arizona Cardinals 33-30 in overtime. In a matchup of the other two teams in the division, the 2-5-1 Washington Commanders defeated the 2-6 Philadelphia Eagles, 27-10.

Cowboys proved who they are in OT loss to Cardinals – Blogging The Boys

The failures were all-around, up, down, forwards, and backwards for the Cowboys after this game, but to be here in week eight with a healthy Dak Prescott having only beaten Marcus Mariota, C.J. Stroud, and Tanner McKee led teams is a failure in preparation and execution that’s very hard to fathom.

Commanders vs. Eagles (game two) – Studs and Duds – Hogs Haven

What a day to be a fan of the [2-4-1 and third in the NFC East] Commanders! In a primetime nationally televised game at home against a division rival, on a day where the Arizona Cardinals came from behind to defeat the Dallas Cowboys in Arlington and the Giants were on a bye, Washington took it to the Eagles at home!

NFL Power Rankings: Big flips since last poll – SB Nation

The NFL is poised to reach the midpoint of the season and we have a good idea how most of the league is shaping up. We’ve got brutal battles in the NFC West and NFC North, with other divisions more or less shaking themselves out — then there’s the NFC South, where seemingly nobody wants to really win. Here are our rankings for Week 8, and then we’ll go over the biggest risers and fallers since our previous rankings.

Browns waive Week 6 TD scorer; have an open roster spot – Dawgs By Nature

Many are hoping the Browns roster looks different because of trades that greatly improve the roster, with defensive end often mentioned as a big need. Smaller moves, like signing [former Eagles] RB Audric Estime off the Minnesota Vikings practice squad a few weeks ago, can have an impact, albeit smaller and for shorter times. In Week 6, with Cleveland’s running back room limited due to injuries, Estime and Jaleel McLaughlin had 18 of the 19 running back carries, split evenly, against the Baltimore Ravens. Estime’s two-yard run was Cleveland’s lone touchdown for the game, but it was enough to help the Browns come away with a victory. Just over two weeks later, Estime is back on waivers:

item.title: Cowboys vs Cardinals: Quinnen Williams shines in demoralizing loss
item.description: At least Quinnen Williams is having individual success these days.
item.content:encoded:
It’s hard to find words to describe what happened to the Dallas Cowboys yesterday. 40 seconds into the fourth quarter, Dallas scored a touchdown to take a 24-10 lead. It hadn’t been pretty, but it looked like the Cowboys were going to finally slay the dragon that is the Arizona Cardinals.

Since 2000, the Cowboys were 69-0 when leading by 14 or more points in the fourth quarter. As has become a theme with this year’s Cowboys team, they continue to make history in the worst way possible. After that Dak Prescott touchdown, Dallas got outscored 23-6, eventually losing the game 33-30 in overtime.

It’s hard to find any positives from such a demoralizing loss, but there were a few players who put together encouraging individual performances. One who stood above the rest was defensive tackle Quinnen Williams. The 28-year-old played like the dominant interior presence Dallas expects him to be, earning him this week’s game ball award.

Williams took advantage of Arizona’s interior offensive line struggles and kept constant pressure on the Cardinals’ pass and run game. Williams led all defenders in the contest with seven total pressures, five QB hurries, and two sacks. His 20% pass-rush win percentage was also the highest among defenders who played 15 or more pass-rush snaps.

Williams didn’t just rush the passer well; he was also arguably Dallas’ best defender against the run. The big defensive tackle totaled three defensive stops, the most of any Cowboys defender, to go with a 23.1% stop percentage. It took a few weeks, but Dallas’ star defensive tackle is starting to look very comfortable in this new defense.

Overall, this was far and away Williams best individual performance of the season to date. While Dallas’ defense as a whole did completely meltdown in the second half, Williams putting together this kind of dominant performance is one bright spot the Cowboys can lean on moving forward.

item.title: Broncos vs. Chiefs: The No Bull Review
item.description: No Bull thoughts, opinions, and analysis on the Denver Broncos’ heart attack win over the Kansas City Chiefs.
item.content:encoded:
Hear me out, Broncos Country. There are a lot of you out there who need to lock in. Eat your veggies, take your vitamins, get some cardio regularly, and don’t forget to mix in some strength resistance training. Especially those of you who, like me, have been watching this team for more than a couple of decades.

The heart attack Broncos are alive and well. 

Mile High Magic lives forever.

Don’t you dare for one second EVER give up on this team. 

From Sean Payton to Bo Nix to Nik Bonitto to the ball boy, this team is built to win come hell or high water. They have absolutely no give-up in them. They are the Rocky Balboa of the NFL, and the Kansas City Chiefs just got knocked the hell out. 

Offense

I’m done getting frustrated with this offense, in all honesty. They had me pulling out my hair for 3 quarters. Constant inability to convert 3rd downs. Giving carries to the objectively worst running back on the team and trotting him out as the starter. Wide receivers who are incapable of getting separation. Tight ends who were paid big bucks to come catch passes and can’t even snag one catch.

My current theory about their ineptness is that Nix is playing it safe to avoid getting buried due to turnovers. He isn’t forcing contested catches unless he has to, for the most part. They believe in their defense to a fault and are very comfortable chipping away until they have to go guns blazing at the end of the game.

Quarterbacks

Bo Nix is my quarterback. I love this guy. The dude can make every throw (whether or not he tries to early in the game). He’s got the most frigid of fluids running in his veins when it gets down to crunch time.

He’s not without faults worth talking about, though. That attempt to throw to Trautman backwards was the most ghastly thing I’ve seen from the Broncos offensive backfield since a Paxton Lynch dab. He also threw a pass into the dirt on 3rd and 10 when Waddle was streaking with plenty of separation from the chaser and the safety.  

He’s also far too timid on 3rd down, throwing short of the sticks. He’s got to work with Payton on how to have reads further down the field that he’s comfortable with at 6, 8, and 10-12 yard depths.

The other thing for him to improve on is navigating throwing windows. He had far too many tipped passes this game, and it cost the team big time on 3rd down.

But man, you have to love that sprinkling of amazing we get to see from him every game. His throw down the sideline to Sutton was perfection. His ability to wait for plays to develop and deliver the ball to open runners gave us big gains by Coleman, Waddle, and Trautman.

Line

The only nit to pick with the line really from this game is training them up on driving into their defenders or chopping their arms when they raise them to bat down passes. I thought the line played very well in this game. Their run blocking has been improving every week. Many of our successful throws were due in large part to excellent blocking up front, giving Nix time to get the ball out.

Running Backs

Jonah Coleman is the truth. He’s a better back than anyone else we have on the roster and needs to take over the starting role immediately. This young man had 11 runs for 41 yards and a touchdown and 4 catches for 63 yards. He’s a power runner who has excellent vision and burst to go with it.

JK Dobbins needs to stop getting a starting role just because he’s a veteran. He certainly does have a run here or there that looks good. The problem is that he gets stuffed for very little gain far too often. He deserved getting benched after losing 8 yards on a run play. This offense is far too fragile for him to try playing Barry Sanders on his Lance Ball skillset.

Receivers

Courtland Sutton may be a bit long in the tooth. He may have lost a step. He put in some great work this week against the Chiefs. Sutton showed supreme focus to catch his long pass over the middle that was tipped by the defender. His sideline go doesn’t look like much on film, but that was a timing route that required him to be in stride between defenders. Sutton caught all 4 of his targets for 53 yards and, as always, had some great blocks in the run game that don’t show up on the stat sheet.

Jaylen Waddle bailed out an awful offensive start after the 8-yard loss by Dobbins by getting a 35-yard pass deep down the middle of the field. He scored his touchdown on a tricky little trips play that had him stutter while Franklin ran upfield in front of him to spring him open for an easy score. He also nailed the 2-point conversion on a deep crossing route behind that caught the deep defender flat-footed.

If you look at the stat sheet, Troy Franklin shouldn’t really be mentioned with 1 of 3 catches for 3 yards. He got us an 18-yard pass interference call, though, and that counts for something in my eyes. Keep grinding, Troy!

Adam Trautman hasn’t gotten as many opportunities this year, but he showed up in this game. He had a big catch downfield for 22 yards after his defender slipped in the 4th quarter and ended the game with 2 catches for 30 yards.

Nate Adkins snuck out into the flat for a TD catch on 4th and goal. I love what Adkins brings to the game. He’s strong as hell as a blocker and is a shifty route runner for a big guy.

Defense

What a gutsy performance from this defense. While they had both their starting corners return for this game, they lost their last standing starting safety when Brandon Jones left the game early. That left them with Taylor Rapp, Devon Key, and JL Skinner holding down the fort at safety. It was a rough go, and Patrick Mahomes took full advantage of the weakness, along with our flaws in coverage from the inside linebacker position.

The Chiefs do a great job against Denver with their quick-throw game, as has been their plan for a few years now. They know their line can’t hold up to the pressure of our defense, which leads Mahomes to get the ball out quickly.

The Chiefs scored 24 and honestly should have scored another 6 to seal the game had they not ultra-choked while poor return coverage, poor pass coverage on Kelce, luck, and practically God himself tried to hand them the game.

But give credit to Vance Joseph and this defense. Bo Nix gets all the talk about comeback wins over the past few years. But none of those stats go in the record books without this defense, and I know Nix would tell you the exact same thing. This defense is absolutely stacked with guys who answer the bell with ice water in their veins when the game is on the line. 

I honestly feel like both Payton and Joseph have a specialty in coaching players on how to execute no matter what. This team knows how to put bad plays behind them and dial in for the next one. We got big plays all over on this defense that found a way to close out this game and get us back on top of the AFC West.

Front 7

Malcolm Roach is a damned playmaker in the trenches, and I don’t think we give him enough credit for how consistent he is up front. While he may have been brought in to stop the run originally, he’s learned how to shed blocks and crash down to get sacks, which we all saw in the last play of the game. He also had a batted pass, tackle for loss, and a quarterback hit in this game to go along with his game-winning sack.

Speaking of that sack, let’s give a quick shout-out to Jonathan Cooper, who is the main reason that sack happened. His rush off the edge was great technical work. He bull-rushed the RT back, stepped into him to make it seem like he was stopped, and then burst out to the left to get around him and force Mahomes upfield into the sack. 

Alex Singleton is still playing his ass off out there. He got smoked for a touchdown early (any play with him in man coverage on a back is a bad design, as he doesn’t have the jets to keep up). He made a key sack right before Butker missed his field goal. It was an excellent job of pressuring up the field without getting fully engaged, which allowed him to dart around the big tackle and put Mahomes in the dirt.

Justin Strnad is usually a wizard in coverage, but he gave up a huge pass to the sideline at the end of the half that set the Chiefs up for a field goal. 

Secondary

Welcome back, Patrick Surtain! He sniffed out a screen early with a big open-field tackle. He also saved a touchdown throw in the end zone with perfect inside leverage coverage. His tackle assist against Walker late in the game was technical perfection on how to take down a big runner if you are a smaller defensive back. He got the outside leg and used his leverage to lift and push to get him down, which was as good a play as his pass defense in the end zone, as both of them stopped a touchdown.

Riley Moss came to play against the Chiefs on Sunday. He put a big-boy hit on Walker, who was running laterally. He barely missed an interception that the receiver had to bat away. I noticed his effort and attention to detail when it came to angles and tackling technique in this game. 

Taylor Rapp gave up a touchdown on a deep pass, looking completely incompetent in the open field. He also had a holding penalty in coverage. While I’m glad for him being available for us to bring in given our injuries at safety (it was an area of weakness I talked about this past offseason), I’m thinking there’s a reason he was available to be signed.

Devon Key needs a ton of love for this game. Key has been a special teams ace for us, but really balled out in this game. He had a pass defense, a tackle for loss, and totaled 8 tackles. 

I usually don’t mention many names of players who had only 9 snaps in the game on defense. Yet on 3rd and goal from the 1-yard line, JL Skinner was in on the left side of the defense assigned to cover Kelce if he went out in a route. The ball was handed off to Walker, who barrelled down the gap next to Skinner. Skinner stood Walker up and put him on the ground. That is a big-time play in a big moment for a guy mainly known as a special teamer.

Special Teams

I thought both Marvin Mims and Cody Schrader did a very good job in the return game for the Broncos. They both averaged at least 25 yards per return and found all the yards that I saw available on their returns.

Unlike the Chiefs (LOL), we have a kicker who knows how to do his job. Wil Lutz was 2 for 2 on field goals and 3 of 3 on extra points. The game didn’t come down to him needing to kick a game-winning field goal, but rest assured, we needed those kicks.

Final Thoughts

Congratulations to Sean Payton for his 200th NFL win. This was a hell of a way to get that notch in your cap. Regardless of how much we nitpick your play calling, let me say that there is no coach I would rather have leading this team than you. Thank you for getting this ship righted and headed in the correct direction. Now let’s keep grinding and see if we can get 12-13 more this season.

I’m not shy about talking about the refs for the KC fans, so let’s address that false start. There are ample videos available out there showing it, as it was the right tackle on the end. He ABSOLUTELY rocked back and turned his body, which is a false start. Yes, he can turn his head, and it doesn’t matter. What matters is that he moved his body. If you don’t want that flag to happen, then he needs to do his damned job and not move before the ball is snapped. Don’t blame the refs for letting it happen other times; blame the player for not having the discipline or intelligence to stop such a dumb habit. It is such a whiny move to say that your team lost because of the refs in this case. That’s not a subjective call at all. Your team deserved to lose that game due to dumb coaching, poor play by your players, and your golden-boy quarterback who melted under the bright lights and pressure.

I will say that I am a big fan of the Broncos buying at the trade deadline. This team needs offense. While Jonah Coleman may be able to provide part of that, there’s no reason not to pursue another talent like Jonathan Taylor or Breece Hall. They instantly improve this offense. The rough part for that is making the money make sense. They will either need to include Dobbins (a rough sell), or cut a player like Evan Engram to get the money to make sense.

Meanwhile, Broncos Country, doesn’t it feel good to be 6-2 at this point in the season? There’s a lot of football left to go. This wasn’t our Super Bowl. We’re a long way from that. Bring on the Panthers.

item.title: Teams are interested in Titans RB Tony Pollard, but Tennessee isn't talking (yet)
item.description: After consistently telling teams that defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons would not be traded, the Titans decided last Tuesday to listen to offers.
item.content:encoded:
After consistently telling teams that defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons would not be traded, the Titans decided last Tuesday to listen to offers.

This Tuesday, they have another decision to make about one of the key offensive players on the roster.

Multiple teams are interested in running back Tony Pollard. So far, however, G.M. Mike Borgonzi has declined to engage in conversations about a potential trade.

Whether that will change remains to be seen, with or without someone calling owner Amy Adams Strunk directly.

Regardless, Pollard is an attractive option for any contender looking for help at the position. His contract is very affordable, relative to the veteran market. His 2027 base salary is $5.99 million (with $3.32 million left for 2026). In 2027, he's due to earn a non-guaranteed base salary of $6.74 million. (In each year, he earns $30,000 for each game in which he's on the active roster.)

Over the past two games, Pollard has rushed for 246 yards and five touchdowns. He's averaging in those two games 5.34 yards per carry.

Pollard has four straight 1,000-yard seasons (two with the Cowboys, two with the Titans). At 595 yards through eight games, he's on pace for a fifth.

With multiple teams linked to Colts running back Jonathan Taylor — and with the Colts not yet in a ballpark that will get a deal done — Pollard could become a much more affordable Plan B as the trade deadline creeps closer and closer.

item.title: Is Lamar Jackson out for the season? Latest injury update on Ravens QB
item.description: Lamar Jackson suffered a serious thumb injury in the Ravens' Week 8 loss to the Bills. Will he miss the remainder of the season? Here's what to know.
item.content:encoded:
The Baltimore Ravenslost starting quarterback Lamar Jackson to a significant thumb injury just one snap into his return from a three-game absence related to an ankle injury.

Jackson was injured in the Ravens' Week 8 game against the Buffalo Bills. He began to attempt his first pass and hit his hand on a Bills defender who was pressuring him off the right side of the offensive line.

Jackson immediately appeared to be in pain and exited the field holding his right hand. He received medical attention on the sideline before being taken to the locker room and quickly ruled out because of the injury. He later returned to the sideline in street clothes, sporting a cast on his injured throwing hand.

Jackson is now staring down another lengthy absence, and the Ravens will have to scramble to replace their star quarterback as they try to remain competitive in the AFC playoff race.

Will Jackson's absence last the remainder of the season? Here's what to know about his status moving forward.

Is Lamar Jackson out for the season?

The Ravens have not officially ruled Jackson out for the remainder of the season. However, coach Jesse Minter did acknowledge the veteran quarterback's thumb injury could "potentially" be season-ending and would land him on IR, at the very least.

"That'll be a surgery deal," Minter said when discussing Jackson's injury during a postgame news conference on Sunday, Nov. 1. "He'll go to IR. That's a tough deal."

Minter was asked again for an update about Jackson's status at a Monday, Nov. 2, media availability. He told reporters the 29-year-old had not yet had surgery and that the team would have more information about his status "maybe sometime this week."

Minter did not share any additional information about Jackson's thumb injury.

"I'm not going to get into the specifics of the injury," Minter told reporters.

How long is Lamar Jackson out?

While Jackson's exact timeline for return remains murky, he will have to miss at least four games once he is placed on IR.

That means the earliest Jackson could potentially return to the field would be in Week 14 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He is guaranteed to miss the Ravens' Weeks 9-12 contests and the team will have a bye in Week 13.

That said, the Ravens will likely have a more definitive timeline for Jackson's return after he has surgery; and it seems possible – if not probable – the two-time MVP will have to miss more than the requisite four games required by an IR stint.

Who will replace Lamar Jackson?

For now, that question remains unsettled. Jackson's normal backup, Tyler Huntley, suffered a turf toe injury while playing in relief of him against the Bills. Huntley seems unlikely to play on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 9, which would push undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into the starting role.

However, Fagnano is dealing with an ankle injury of his own suffered against the Bills. Minter acknowledged the 25-year-old may "have a chance to play" against the Jacksonville Jaguars, but wouldn't commit to him making the start.

"I think we'll figure that out over the next day or two," Minter said.

The Ravens added two quarterbacks to their organization ahead of their Thursday night game. Initially, they signed Austin Reed, who spent time with the team during the preseason, to their practice squad on Monday. The following day, they poached Kedon Slovis from the Green Bay Packers' squad, guaranteeing the team will have at least two fully healthy quarterbacks available for their Week 9 game.

Ravens QB depth chart

Below is a look at the current state of the Ravens' quarterback depth chart

  1. Lamar Jackson (injured)
  2. Tyler Huntley (injured)
  3. Joe Fagnano
  4. Austin Reed (practice squad)
  5. Kedon Slovis

Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and an interception in relief of Jackson and Huntley against the Bills. The 6-3, 230-pound signal-caller spent the final three seasons of his college career at UConn and completed 68% of his passes for 3,448 yards, 28 touchdowns and one interception during his sixth and final college season.

Like Fagnano, Reed was an undrafted free agent who joined the Chicago Bears in 2024. The Western Kentucky product has not yet appeared in an NFL regular-season game, but he thrived for the Dallas Renegades during the 2026 UFL season, completing 56.3% of his passes for 1,923 yards, a league-high 21 touchdowns and nine interceptions.

Slovis is another player who went undrafted in 2024. The USC, Pitt and BYU product spent time with four NFL teams before joining the Ravens from the Packers' practice squad. He dressed for two games with the Arizona Cardinals last season and completed 1 of 2 passes for negative-2 yards.

Because Slovis was on the Packers' practice squad, the Ravens needed to sign him to their 53-man roster to obtain him ahead of Thursday's game. That said, the 25-year-old will likely remain behind Reed given that the latter spent time with Baltimore during the preseason – though Slovis previously played for Ravens quarterback coach Israel Woolfork in Arizona.

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Is Lamar Jackson out for the season? Latest injury update on Ravens QB
